question: An excessive amount of cadmium in the human body causes:
solution:
The correct answer is__** itai-itai.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Itai-itai disease is caused by cadmium (Cd) exposure, produced as a result of human activities related to industrialization. 
 
• It was first recognized in Japan in the 1960s.
 
• Itai-itai disease is characterized by osteomalacia with severe bone pain and is associated with renal tubular dysfunction.
 
• This disease was recognized as the** Four Big Pollution Diseases of Japan.**
 
• Cadmium is a naturally occurring** toxic heavy metal.**
 
• It is an extremely toxic industrial and environmental** pollutant classified as a human carcinogen.**
 
• It is used in the manufacturing of NiCd rechargeable batteries.
